newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Report says Telecom buyback scheme fair.
newsitem.headline: Report says Telecom buyback scheme fair.

text.p: An appraisal report prepared by County NatWest Securities New Zealand Ltd and published on Tuesday said that Telecom's NZ$1 billion share buyback scheme was fair to non-associated shareholders of Telecom.
The report said there was sufficient disclosure to enable all shareholders to understand the relevant factors and make an informed decision.
Telecom announced in November it planned a NZ$1 billion share repurchase programme over one year starting in the fourth quarter of its 1996/97 fiscal year.

Half the shares would be purchased on the New Zealand and New York stock exchanges and the other half would be repurchased directly from Ameritech and Bell Atlantic, which each own a quarter of the company.
Telecom has 1.89 billion shares on issue.
The repurchase involves buying a maximum of 80 million shares on-market.
Repurchases would be restricted to periods when the board was satisfied all material information was known to shareholders.
The market would be informed on a daily basis about purchases.
Prices paid by Ameritech and Bell would be the weigthed average of repurchases made on market on the relevant day.
